# ShannonBase Repository Summary

## What It Does

**ShannonBase** is a MySQL fork positioned as "The Next-Gen Database for AI" and "the MySQL of the AI era." Its core pitch is consolidating the entire modern AI application stack into a single engine: instead of chaining MySQL → ETL → Vector DB → Feature Store → Inference Server → App, you get OLTP + OLAP + Vector + ML Training + LLM Inference + RAG + Agents in one database. Everything is doable **in SQL** with "zero extra infrastructure."

## Tech Stack

- **Base:** MySQL 8.0 wire-protocol compatible (fork of MySQL 8.4.x; currently tracking 8.4.11)
- **Language:** Primarily C/C++ (inherited from MySQL codebase)
- **Build:** CMake
- **Embedded runtimes:**
  - ONNX Runtime (local LLM inference)
  - JerryScript (JavaScript stored procedures)
  - LightGBM / XGBoost (in-database ML training)
- **License:** GPL-2.0

## Architecture

- **Dual-engine HTAP:** InnoDB (row store) + **Rapid** in-memory columnar engine, synced via redo log / DML notification with cost- and ML-based query routing
- **Native vector support:** First-class `VECTOR` data type and distance functions
- **"Rapid" engine internals** (from commit messages): IMCS/IMCU storage, ART indexes, WAL replay, snapshot checkpoints, compression (LZ4/zlib/zstd), hash-join spilling, parallel scanning
- **Agent engine:** Built-in agent execution framework runnable via SQL, with per-user scoping and approval gates for writes/DDL
- **ML/Tooling layer** exposed through `sys.ML_*` functions and JavaScript procedures

# Mega2: Monorepo Engine and Git Server for AI Agents

[](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2#mega2-monorepo-engine-and-git-server-for-ai-agents)

> An open-source, trunk-based monorepo storage and Git hosting server written in Rust, with Git Smart HTTP, Git LFS, an OCI container registry, build-artifact storage, and Agent Session Capture.

The first-generation [Mega](https://github.com/web3infra-foundation/mega) established the foundation for our monorepo and Git-hosting platform. **Mega2 is the second-generation engine built for AI agents**, with two core capabilities: a **Monorepo engine** and **Agent Session Capture**.

The open-source edition of Mega2 runs in **trunk / storage-only** mode and does not include a Web UI or Change List. Mega2 provides the server-side monorepo storage and APIs; Libra provides a terminal interface for interactive browsing.

Start with the [Quick Start](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/quick-start.md), then see the [documentation index](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/README.md) for user, operator, and contributor guides. Repository and push behavior is covered in the [User Guide](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md); contribution checks are in the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/contributing.md).

## At a glance

[](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2#at-a-glance)

Item Details What it is Monorepo engine and Git hosting server for AI agents Website [gitmega.ai](https://gitmega.ai) Language Rust (edition 2024), a single Cargo package `mega2` Mode Trunk / storage-only: `refs/heads/main` is the public trunk Protocols and interfaces Git Smart HTTP, read-only SSH, Git LFS, OCI Distribution (`/v2`), HTTP API API docs OpenAPI: `/api/openapi.json`; Swagger UI: `/swagger-ui` Storage Postgres for metadata; local filesystem or S3-compatible object storage for Git objects, LFS, artifacts, and images Image Docker Hub [`genedna/mega2`](https://hub.docker.com/r/genedna/mega2), default HTTP port `9000` Not included Web UI, Change List, multi-branch monorepo workflows Companion tools [Libra](https://libra.tools) (agent-side version control and terminal browser), [ScorpioFS](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/scorpiofs) (monorepo filesystem mount) License MIT OR Apache-2.0

## Recommended Agent setup

[](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2#recommended-agent-setup)

The best practice for agent-oriented monorepo development is to use **Mega2 + ScorpioFS + Libra** together:

- **Mega2** provides centralized monorepo storage and hosting, with optional Agent Session Capture.
- [**ScorpioFS**](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/scorpiofs) mounts remote monorepo paths as a local filesystem for development tools and agents to browse.
- [**Libra**](https://libra.tools) provides agent-side version-control workflows and a terminal browser for Mega2.

Use `libra mega2 browser --server https://mega2.example.com` to browse a remote monorepo. The terminal interface displays one directory level at a time, supports creating, deleting, moving, and renaming directories, and has a Tag panel for listing, creating, and deleting root tags; write credentials are required to create or delete tags. This command reads remote tree data; it does not run Git clone, fetch, or push. See [Using Mega2 with Libra](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md#6-using-mega2-with-libra).

## Core capabilities

[](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2#core-capabilities)

### Monorepo engine

[](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2#monorepo-engine)

Mega2 provides trunk-based Git storage and hosting for monorepos. Regular Monorepo paths expose `refs/heads/main` as the public trunk; Git clients cannot push other branches or tags. Use the HTTP API or Libra's terminal browser for supported Tag and directory operations. The open-source edition does not include the multi-branch Change List feature.

Git metadata is stored in Postgres, while Git objects live in local or S3-compatible object storage. ImportRepos under `[monorepo].import_dir` (default `/third-party`) follow ordinary Git semantics, including multiple branches and client-managed tags, and can hold third-party repositories that need independent synchronization. ImportRepos accept later pushes (branches and tags) and can be removed through `POST /api/v1/import-repo/remove` (which needs a push token; `push_auth=none` deployments run `mega2 import-repo remove` on the server instead); see [ImportRepo lifecycle](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md#26-importrepo-lifecycle). See [Monorepo path policy and first use](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md#25-monorepo-path-policy-and-first-use) for path provisioning and push rules.

### Agent Session Capture

[](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2#agent-session-capture)

Agent Session Capture is an optional HTTP capability, separate from Git push. When enabled with `[agent_capture].enabled=true` and an ingest token in a storage-only deployment, Mega2 can capture agent sessions, events, checkpoints, file operations, and transcript data for later querying, review, and audit. Git branch and receive-pack rules do not govern this API. See the [Configuration Guide](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/configuration.md) for setup.

## Other capabilities

[](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2#other-capabilities)

- **Git and large files**: Git Smart HTTP supports clone, fetch, pull, and push; SSH is read-only in storage-only mode; Git LFS is supported.
- **Build artifacts and OCI**: Artifact Sets store build outputs. When `[oci].enabled=true`, the `/v2` endpoint provides an OCI container registry. Git, LFS, Artifact, and OCI data can share object storage.
- **HTTP API**: Read and write monorepo files, directories, and tags. See the [User Guide](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/user-guide.md) for the API and workflows.
- **Security and operations**: Push-token authentication, embedded Vault and SecretRef, webhook notifications, and configuration validation, profiles, and controlled hot reload. See the [Configuration Guide](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/configuration.md) and [Deployment Guide](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/deployment.md).

## Quick start with Compose

[](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2#quick-start-with-compose)

The evaluation stack pulls the official release image from Docker Hub (`genedna/mega2:latest`) — no source build, no bootstrap, and no clone of the mega2 source repository. Download the compose file for your platform from gitmega.ai and start it from the same directory (the two files differ in how artifact presigned URLs are made reachable from the host — see the [Deployment Guide](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/deployment.md)):

```
# macOS with OrbStack
curl -fsSLO https://gitmega.ai/macos-orbstack-mega2-compose.yml
docker compose -f macos-orbstack-mega2-compose.yml up -d --wait
# Linux Docker
curl -fsSLO https://gitmega.ai/linux-mega2-compose.yml
docker compose -f linux-mega2-compose.yml up -d --wait
```

gitmega.ai serves this repository's root [`macos-orbstack-mega2-compose.yml`](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/macos-orbstack-mega2-compose.yml) and [`linux-mega2-compose.yml`](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/linux-mega2-compose.yml); in a checkout of this repository, skip the download and run `docker compose` directly.

HTTP: `http://127.0.0.1:9000/`. This is a local-only anonymous setup (`push_auth=none`, bound to `127.0.0.1`); for token-based or shared deployments see the [Deployment Guide](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/deployment.md) and [`docs/deploy-trunk.md`](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/deploy-trunk.md) (Chinese). Start and push with the [Quick Start](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/quick-start.md), then see [Usage Recipes](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/recipes.md) for repository migration, LFS, OCI, and build-artifact examples.

For local development and tests, see the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/contributing.md).

### Stop

[](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2#stop)

Run this from the directory that holds the compose file. The `-v` flag deletes data stored in the Docker volumes.

```
docker compose -f macos-orbstack-mega2-compose.yml down -v   # or linux-mega2-compose.yml
```

## Contributing

[](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2#contributing)

For a large change, follow this process:

1. **Open an issue.** Describe the problem, motivation, scope, and non-goals. Get agreement on the direction before implementation.
2. **Then write a plan.** Copy the structure from the [English Plan Template](https://github.com/gitmono-dev/mega2/blob/main/docs/plan/plan-template.en.md) into `docs/plan/plan-YYYYMMDD.md`. Do not delete mandatory sections; write `N/A` and the reason when a section does not apply.
3. **Implement only after the plan is reviewed.** Split work into task cards, add tests and docs, and pass the submit gates before merge.

A plan is not an implementation. When drafting one, verify assumptions against the current source, tests, config, and docs. Agreements in an issue do not replace the task card's verification commands.

Before submitting code, run:

```
cargo +nightly fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
source .env.test && cargo test --all
```

# Spatial Memory Engine (SME) — Repository Summary

## What It Does
SME is a **long-term memory plugin for AI applications**. Unlike traditional vector databases that only do `Memory → Embedding → TopK` storage, SME organizes memories into a **self-evolving spatial space** — positioning itself as a next-gen memory engine that turns an AI "from forgetting after each chat into understanding you better the more you talk to it."

It is benchmarked **head-to-head against Mem0 and bare RAG**, and is **Chinese-friendly** and **offline-capable with zero config**.

---

## Tech Stack
- **Language:** Python ≥ 3.10 (Windows / Linux)
- **Core dependencies:** `numpy`, `httpx`, `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `networkx`, `python-multipart`, `hnswlib`
- **Optional extras:**
  - `[ann]` — hnswlib ANN acceleration
  - `[local-embeddings]` — sentence-transformers (e.g., `BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5`)
  - `[viz]` — matplotlib for visualization
  - `[onnx]` — fastembed (ONNX int8, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B)
  - `[mcp]` — MCP protocol (mcp ≥ 2.0)
- **LLM/Embedding:** Any OpenAI-compatible service (cloud or local); built-in hashing embedding for zero-dependency offline use

---

## Architecture
- **`sme/`** — core engine, config registry (97 config items), models, memory manager
- **`space/`** — density-driven **Memory Regions** (auto grow/split/merge, graph-connected)
- **`retrieval/`** — two-stage hybrid retrieval (vector / Chinese bigram BM25 / metadata + optional graph expansion + 8-signal explainable ranking)
- **`dynamics/`** — Ebbinghaus reinforcement, time decay, consolidation, compression, archive, policy
- **`modules/`** — 12 extension modules (fact extraction, QA pairs, temporal knowledge graph, profiles, fact versioning, noise suppression, WAL persistence, storage backends, REST+SDK, observability, layered context, multi-user namespaces)
- **`storage/`** — snapshots, backends, write-ahead log (WAL)
- **`api/`** — FastAPI REST server + official client + Web config center
- **`lab/`**, **`docs/`** — experiments/benchmarks and documentation
- **Memory Graph** — six semantic edge types (reference/causal/dialogue/summary/parent-child/neighbor)

---

## Stars

---

## Key Features
| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Zero-config offline** | Built-in hashing embedding, no keys needed |
| **Explainable retrieval** | Every hit carries an 8-signal `breakdown` (semantic/importance/freshness/weight/decay/hit_count/recency/region) |
| **Chinese-friendly** | Bigram BM25 keyword channel (on by default) + document chunk import |
| **Memory lifecycle** | Reinforcement/decay/merge/compression configurable; memories never deleted by decay; archives recoverable |
| **Fully toggleable** | 97 config items + 5 presets (chat assistant / dynamic KB / static KB / embodied robot / all-off) |
| **Multiple access modes** | Python SDK, REST API + client, MCP (one-line mount), Web config center |
| **Retrieval 1.3** | Min-max hybrid fusion (+2.5–4.2pp acc), Personalized PageRank graph expansion (HippoRAG 2 path), optional sleep-time compute, ONNX int8 |
| **Performance** | WAL 2557 writes/s (1.79x); ONNX batch 7.4x; graph hot-path 127–159x; hashing search p50 ~4ms (2k entries) |

---

## README Highlights
- **Two-stage hybrid retrieval:** Region-led recall + hybrid vector/BM25/metadata + optional graph enhancement + explainable 8-signal ranking.
- **Benchmark results (lab/战报.md):**
  - **96.7%** accuracy on the arena test (3 seeds × 60 rounds × 40 questions, LLM blind-judged) vs Mem0 / bare RAG / BM25 / Graphiti — lowest distraction (only 2 times).
  - **Scale interference:** SME holds ~90% at 2000 noise memories; BM25 degrades to 82.5%.
  - **Region ablation (honest note):** Region removal changes accuracy by 0–1pp (within noise) — the anti-interference gain comes from hybrid retrieval + memory dynamics; both were falsified from the original attribution. Region's proven value is that **retrieval latency stays flat** as the library grows (235ms flat vs +21% degradation when disabled).
  - **Long-range test:** SME improves 92.5% → 95% across replays; bare RAG declines 92.5% → 87.5% (7.5pp structural gap).
- **Quick start (10 seconds):** `SpatialMemoryEngine()` with no config; `add` / `search` / `reinforce` / `visualize` / `save` / `load` in a few lines.
- **Web config center:** `python -m sme.api` then open `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` — 97 items in 9 groups, one-click presets, live validation, hot rebuild on save.
- **LLM provider table:** OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, OpenRouter, SiliconFlow, vLLM, LM Studio, Ollama.
- **Security:** Zero keys by default; saved config in gitignored `data/`; REST mode keys via environment variables (not persisted).
- **License:** Apache-2.0.
- **Latest commit:** Oct 9, 2026 — namespace alignment (REST first-class `ns` param, MCP optional `ns`), plus honest attribution corrections in the README.

**One-line pitch:** *Turn your AI from "forgets after chatting" into "understands you better the more you talk."*

# Morphz Repository Summary

## Overview
**Morphz** is an open-source **agent runtime** developed by **Newvar** for persistent cognition, structured context, and concurrent work.

**Core thesis:** *"From Chat Completion to Structured Context Evaluation."* Rather than feeding a growing chat transcript to a language model, Morphz makes **structured Context** the object the model evaluates directly. # Kestrel (红隼) — Repository Summary

## What It Does

Kestrel is a **pure C11, zero-third-party-dependency inference engine** for ARM aarch64 CPUs. It runs multiple model types natively on edge devices — no GPU/NPU required — from a single ~1.4 MB binary. RK3588 (Orange Pi 5 Plus) is the primary development/benchmark platform, but the engine targets any ARMv8.2-A device with NEON dotprod/fp16.

A single process serves **five model families** behind an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API:

| Model family | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Qwen3-VL 2B / 8B | Text + image/video |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE) | Large MoE LLM |
| Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B | Vector embeddings |
| Laya (ModernBERT-large) | Decision model (non-autoregressive) |
| YOLO v5/v8/v11 | Object detection |

The project is version **v1.0 (test release)** and marketed as "native small-model inference + Chinese national-cryptography trusted computing."

## Tech Stack

- **Language:** C11 — 28 C source files, single project / single artifact
- **Build:** CMake + `build_rk3588.sh` (native, `--run-tests`, `--static`, `--cross`)
- **Runtime deps:** none — standard build needs only gcc + libm; static build produces zero `.so` dependencies
- **Included third-party code (MIT, file-head attributed only):** `stb_image.h` (image decoding) and a llama.cpp-derived 4x4 asm GEMM kernel
- **Custom-built:** NEON quantized GEMM/GEMV, custom thread pool `vllm_tp` (replaces OpenMP), national crypto (SM3/SM4/SM2), VQF v2 mmap format, NPU direct driver (`/dev/rknpu`)
- **Optional:** NPU acceleration via stock rknpu kernel UAPI (register-command self-test required; falls back to CPU); FHE (RNS-CKKS) ciphertext inference chain drivers

## Architecture

```
include/ src/
  core/    — inference kernels (NTT/FHE/CKKS/tp/matmul/attention/L3)
  model/   — weight loading (VQF v2 mmap only), vision, tokenization
  serve/   — HTTP / admin UI / batching / attestation
  media/   — H.264/MP4 decoding (independent, disabled by default)
tools/     — bench, build, client, ops, security, npu, kernels, preproc,
             drivers (FHE), relay (community compute chain)
vqf_convert/ — standalone safetensors/GGUF → VQF v2 converter
docs/      — Chinese technical docs, benchmark reports, pre-registrations
```

**Serving surface:** `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/systemone` (Laya), `/v1/detect` (YOLO), orchestration via `/v1/scene`, `/v1/rag`, and a unified `/v1/ask` endpoint that routes on explicit fields only (`image`→scene, `kb_dir`→rag, `questions`→decide, else chat), returning a `route` field.

## Key Features

1. **VQF single-file weights** — self-designed format, mmap-direct with on-demand paging. v1 dropped GGUF/safetensors loading; conversion moved to the bundled `vqf_convert/` tool.
2. **Layer-streaming inference** (`VLLM_VQF_STREAM=1`) — weights paged in per-layer then `MADV_DONTNEED`; resident RSS decoupled from model size. Measured savings: **4.6× / 8.9× / 23.2×** (2B / 8B / 30B-A3B). Enables running 17.67 GB 30B-A3B on a 16 GB board. Semantics unchanged (bit-identical TOKIDS). *Limitation: plaintext VQF only — encrypted/signed weights rejected.*
3. **KV v2 lazy allocation + L3 tiered residency + P3** — L3 eviction coexists with prefix reuse, cutting multi-turn prefill by **−80% to −96%**.
4. **Rule packs (pre-built contexts)** — recurrent fixed manuals cached as reusable prefixes; short manual (5,791 tokens) shows ≈82× speedup; >8K-token manuals not persisted.
5. **Sparse attention length gating** — decode (default on-trigger at 1024): 1.58×/2.16×/2.92× at 4K/8K/16K; prefill (3072): +18.4% at 1K, turns positive at 4.4K, −45% at 16K. Both axes default **off**.
6. **Verifiable inference (attestation)** — SM2 supply-chain signing + per-request attestation (schema 3, binds request body via SM3); verified in-browser or offline via zero-dependency Python tool.
7. **Weight protection** — VQF-Enc (SM4-CTR + HMAC-SM3) and embedded SM2 signatures, stackable.
8. **MoE expert parallelism (EP)** — shards experts across machines; outputs bit-identical across ranks. ⚠️ No auth/integrity on the EP wire protocol — trusted networks only.
9. **x86-64 port** — functional/consistency self-check only, explicitly **not** for performance baselines.

## README Highlights

**Performance positioning (2026-09-12 v1 measurements, RK3588):**

- **30B-A3B vs prior version:** decode **1.74–3.72×** faster; prefill 1.21× (cold) to 5.44× (hot). Memory flat.
- **8B:** unchanged in v1 — dense model is bandwidth-bound, and the v1 optimizations target compute cost instead (MoE gains don't apply). Author honestly flags that the bandwidth-bound explanation still *needs a measured confirmation*.
- **8B vs llama.cpp** (same weights, same 4-bit, both optimized): prefill loses 1.32× at 2K but reverses to 1.60× ahead at 16K; decode reverses from 1.07× (2K) to 3.63× (16K); multi-turn reuse leads **1.33–3.4×** across all contexts.
- **Recommended config is 8B**, threads **4** (using 8 threads pulls in the A55 little cores and slows decode 1.8–2.5×): 8.7× memory saving, hot TTFT median 1.734 s, tpot median 330.2 ms, ±0.26% variance across 5 samples.
- **30B is a capability-ceiling tier, not a recommendation** — weights exceed page cache; usable mode is thinking-off + short context (~20.8 s for a complete short answer); default thinking needs 300+ tokens and 3–4 minutes per turn.

**Notable README style — rigorous measurement discipline:**

- Strict version partitioning: v0 numbers (2026-09-05) explicitly declared **unusable** for v1 conclusions; the entire 2026-09-12 historical dataset **retracted** because it couldn't be reproduced from the same commit (different binary + session state).
- Three separate measurement categories kept unmixable: controlled A/B (within 1%), single-shot serve measurements, and cross-engine fair A/B.
- **Pre-registration** docs — criteria frozen before looking at data; controlled alternation within a session; temperature/frequency continuously logged (no thermal throttling observed).
- Explicit "honest boundaries" section listing every caveat: encrypted weights can't stream, EP is unauthenticated, 32K/64K untested, 2B lineage retired due to quantization mismatch.

**Licensing:** **Apache-2.0** as of v1.0 (previously AGPL-3.0-or-later / commercial dual license) — permits closed-source integration and SaaS. Prior commits and releases remain irrevocably AGPL.

**Notable gaps / honest caveats:** architecture support is narrow (Qwen3 family only — Llama and older Qwen explicitly unverified); FHE layer-chain has only 23 of 28 layers completed with community compute still being solicited; cold-start figures (2.0 s) and llama.cpp startup/RSS comparisons are v0-only and have not been re-measured for v1.

场景 具体处理 已验证范围 正常模型发布与多版本更新 检查受支持格式；复用同一内容、同一扫描器版本的完整文件证据；每个提交生成自己的报告 真实 BERT-Tiny 权重、同模型派生分片、README-only 更新；另有合成 1 GiB 容量文件 模型加载可能执行代码 结合杀毒与静态反序列化检查；记录危险引用；服务端拒绝风险版本下载；人工意见不能解除阻断 受控无害风险夹具、真实 API 下载拒绝、旧安全提交仍可下载 文件不完整或证据失效 截断、坏构造参数、未支持语义不冒充完整检查；规则版本变化后不继承旧许可 当前应用中的不完整版本、同提交 scanner generation 切换、独立大文件前缀诊断

## [](https://gitee.com/lin-lab/matrixhub-model-security#%E5%AE%9E%E7%8E%B0%E4%B8%8E%E8%B4%A1%E7%8C%AE%E8%BE%B9%E7%95%8C)实现与贡献边界

```
HF/API 上传 → 固定提交与文件清单 → 有界暂存/前缀预检
                                   ↓
                         隔离 ClamAV + 静态格式检查
                                   ↓
                         完整证据 + generation + 策略
                                   ↓
                         服务端下载准入 → UI/审计/复核
```

- **隔离检查**：扫描服务在受限 Linux 环境中工作；不通过 `torch.load`、`pickle.load` 或执行文件指定的构造函数来判断安全。
- **有限语义检查**：对支持的 CPU legacy tensor 构造参数、storage 长度、形状、步长与偏移进行静态验证。未知或不完整语义保持不完整状态，不能当作无风险批准。
- **提前拒绝**：暂存时可用前 64 KiB 判断部分 legacy 元数据已不合格。结果只有拒绝或待定，不能生成放行证据。
- **跨文件流水线**：准备下一批文件的同时扫描上一批已完成的快照；资源有上限，取消后先等待扫描退出再清理。
- **多版本缓存**：内容、大小、类型、范围和 scanner generation 匹配且旧结果完整时，复用分析。仍先完整读取文件、计算摘要并生成扫描快照；省去重复分析，再生成本次提交的报告。
- **服务端准入**：证据绑定不可变提交与当前扫描器版本；风险、不完整、缺失或过期结果不能通过受保护下载绕过。
- **人工复核**：Editor/Admin 可追加确认风险、疑似误报或跟进意见；记录绑定报告和身份，追加审计，不改变机器报告、缓存或下载判断。

**ClamAV 与 Picklescan 是第三方开源引擎，并非本项目原创。** 本项目的工作是模型格式检查增强、隔离集成、证据与版本约束、扫描调度和业务准入。当前锁定 ClamAV 1.4.6、Picklescan 1.0.5；没有宣称优化了 ClamAV 内核或发现全部未知威胁。

本次公开目录保留原始证据中的少量本机路径元数据。冻结源码里的旧报告、旧环境与镜像说明属于历史记录；当前版本与验收以根目录版本锁和最终报告为准，详见 [发布说明](https://gitee.com/lin-lab/matrixhub-model-security/blob/main/PUBLICATION_NOTES.md)。

# LayerTrace (层迹) — Repository Summary

## What It Does

LayerTrace is a **cross-layer fault diagnosis system** for AI workloads running on virtual machines. Its core value proposition: starting from a failed AI task, it uses a traceable evidence chain to distinguish between three different failure causes:

1. **Container process anomalies**
2. **Model compute resource bottlenecks**
3. **Tool/service failures**

It is built with the **VM as the boundary**, capturing evidence across the container, model, and tool-service layers. States are explicitly labeled as **replay / observation / inference / unknown** to keep evidence provenance clear.

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technologies / Details |
|---|---|
| **Language** | Python 3.12 |
| **Deployment** | Docker + Compose plugin; Linux x86_64 |
| **Database** | PostgreSQL 16.4 (with Alembic migrations — `alembic.ini`) |
| **Monitoring** | Prometheus 3.5.0; optional Grafana, Tempo, Caddy |
| **Model Runtime** | llama.cpp (MIT) with Qwen GGUF models (Apache-2.0); requires AVX2 CPU |
| **Testing** | pytest (`pytest.ini`) |
| **Platform Integration** | ZSvirt (read-only adapter) |
| **License** | Apache-2.0 |

## Architecture

The system breaks into several deployable tiers:

- **Control Plane + Web UI** — central orchestration, authenticated API, browser login form and Bearer-token machine clients

# ContextStore Repository Summary

## What It Does

**ContextStore** is a tiered shared storage system for **LLM inference KV caches**. It extends the KV cache beyond a single node's GPU HBM into a hierarchy of storage tiers:
- GPU HBM (L1)
- Host memory (L2)
- Local NVMe (L3)
- Remote JBOF / NVMe-oF pools (L3 distributed)

The core benefit: it enables **cross-instance, cross-session KV reuse** for inference workers (vLLM, Dynamo). Long-context and multi-replica deployments avoid repeating expensive prefill computation on cache-warm prefixes.

---

## Technology Stack

| Component | Path | Language | Role |
|-----------|------|----------|------|
| **ContextStore Connector** | `src/contextstore/` | Python | vLLM/Dynamo `KVConnector` plugin; owns codec, prefix index, scheduler/worker split, tiered cache, KVService client |
| **KVService** | `kv-service/` | Rust | Standalone distributed block-storage service for JBOF/NVMe-oF; exposes gRPC + RDMA data paths |
| **NIXL Plugin** | `nixl-plugin/` | C++ / Rust | Loads ContextStore as NIXL's `CONTEXTSTORE` backend under the `OBJ` descriptor contract |

**Supporting infrastructure:** Redis (placement/metadata store), io_uring + O_DIRECT (NVMe I/O), protobuf/gRPC.

---

## Architecture

The system is split into **independently built and deployed parts**:

```
vLLM/Dynamo ──┬──> ContextStore Connector ─┐
              ├──> External KV mgr (client-rs) ─┤
              └──> NIXL Plugin ─────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
              KVService Cluster (multi-node)
              ┌── node A ──┐  ┌── node B ──┐
              │ MemoryTier │  │ MemoryTier │
              │ StorageTier│  │ StorageTier│
              └────────────┘  └────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
                       Redis (placement metadata)
```

**Key architectural principles:**
- **Consumer-agnostic service:** KVService is independent of any consumer. External KV managers integrate via the Rust SDK (`kv-service/client-rs`) or gRPC API directly (e.g., redhare's cold-tier backend).
- **Separated concerns:** Consumers own KV semantics; KVService owns shared capacity, cross-node striping, and data paths.
- **Striping:** Objects above a size threshold are striped across nodes and disks; readers pull each node's stripes concurrently.
- **Descriptor-based reads:** `LookupObject` returns a descriptor (no payload); `ReadByDescriptor` fetches payload. Enables client-cached descriptors and single-round-trip hot GETs via speculative concurrent lookup+read.

---

## Key Features

### Storage & Data Path
- **Object store model** with `ObjectKey{namespace, object_key}` and opaque server-generated metadata (handles, generations, content ETags, layout versions, striping info).
- **RDMA data path** with multi-endpoint stripe-subset GETs and optional **SGE scatter direct-write** (server writes straight into scattered client buffers, no staging copy).
- **Pre-registered RDMA slabs** and zero-memcpy RDMA WRITE for the JBOF path.
- **io_uring + O_DIRECT** NVMe access with pooled aligned read buffers to avoid first-touch page faults.

### Performance (documented benchmarks)
- **2 nodes × 2 NVMe** (fio ceiling ~28 GB/s): **6.4–8.8 GB/s** per synchronous client stream, **23 GB/s** aggregate at 8 concurrent streams.
- Streaming PUT pipeline: server-side throughput improved from 0.65 → **1.5–1.9 GiB/s** (1 GiB object).
- Aggregate GET improved from 0.71 → **3.0–3.3 GB/s** (8×512 MB cold reads).
- Pooled O_DIRECT buffers: per-stripe read latency dropped from 50–180 ms cold to **18–20 ms** warm.

### Reliability & Correctness
- **Speculative concurrent lookup + read:** hot GETs stay at one round trip; handles concurrent overwrite/rebalance correctly (ETag + layout_version validation with `FAILED_PRECONDITION` recovery).
- **Generation-based garbage collection** and optional **stripe integrity checks**.
- **Multi-endpoint HA** support (pass a list of endpoints instead of one).

### Deployment Flexibility
- Local dev (TOML config + local NVMe)
- Docker / Compose
- **Kubernetes** (three manifests: gRPC-only, RDMA hostNetwork, RDMA over Multus/spiderpool secondary NIC)
- **Systemd** with hardened baremetal toolkit (immutable release dirs, atomic activation, acceptance checklist)
- **JBOF over NVMe-oF** (SPDK target + initiator helpers)

# RailFuse in ContextStore: Summary

## Where It Appears

The README contains **three sections** directly relevant to RailFuse / multi-rail, with several more linked docs (not inlined):

| Location | Content |
|---|---|
| **Top of README** — "RailFuse competition entry and demonstration (2026-10-16 V4)" | Project intro, demo video, presenter guide, illustration/review bundle, workflow skill, live-demo receipts, FFI safety acceptance |
| **"Multi-rail descriptor reads (experimental)"** | The core technical documentation (route semantics, safety, benchmarks, fault injection, Soft-RoCE VM reproduction) |
| **"Research branch: direct ordered private staging"** | Performance results and safety contract for the ordered-staging mechanism |

Linked (but not inlined) docs that likely mention RailFuse/multi-rail include `docs/story.md`, `docs/multi-rail-design.md`, `docs/rail-capability-discovery.md`, the Chinese research summary (`中文研究摘要与验收边界…`), and the paper figures/safety contract.

> Note: The term **"多轨"** (Chinese for "multi-rail") does not literally appear in the README text itself, but it is the Chinese term for the multi-rail concept and is the subject of the Chinese-language PDF docs (project introduction, demo guide, research summary) linked in the README.

---

## What RailFuse Does

### Core Idea
**RailFuse** is a fork/research branch of ContextStore that adds **object-aware multi-rail client reads**. ContextStore itself is tiered shared storage for LLM inference KV caches (spilling KV from GPU HBM → host memory → NVMe → remote NVMe-oF/JBOF). RailFuse's contribution is a **client-side reader** that reads a single striped object across **multiple local RDMA devices ("rails")** to squeeze more bandwidth from one storage node.

### The Three Decisions (the "story")
1. **Plan the paths** — decide how object stripes are scheduled across rails
2. **Validate before publication** — verify descriptor/placement identity and checksums before any bytes are exposed
3. **Retire DMA ownership before reuse** — tear down QP/MR before buffers can be reused (fail-stop on uncertain completions)

### Key Capabilities
- **`RailReader`** — reads one striped object over multiple local RDMA devices and listeners on the *same owning storage node*. Uses the existing descriptor GET + tag-15 SGE scatter protocol; **object placement and disk stripes are unchanged**.
- **Rail discovery** — `RailReader::discover_from_placement` matches server-advertised "fabric/listener capabilities" (attached to `Placement`) with locally configured device/port/GID paths. Old clients ignore the extra protobuf field; explicit `RailRoute` configs still work with old servers.
- **Weighted scheduling** — a 7th rail field sets a positive relative weight (default 1); NUMA node and PCI address are reported from sysfs when available.
- **Direct ordered private staging (research branch)** — opt-in `RailLimits::direct_staging` + `contiguous_schedule`: eligible single-owner striped objects write disjoint slices of one request-private ordered buffer. Defaults to `false`; other placements fall back to the existing packed path.

### Safety / Correctness Guarantees
- Descriptor + placement identity rechecked **after** transfer; bytes published only after **all rails and available checksums** succeed.
- **Failed/cancelled reads leave the caller buffer unchanged.**
- Cancellation and publishing share a gate (first-to-start wins).
- Per-rail registered receive buffer; bounds on concurrent tasks and in-flight bytes per rail.
- Registered-memory budget capped at **80% of soft `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK`**.
- Uncertain CQ completion **terminates the connection** rather than reusing the CQ; a GET control error destroys the QP so late replies can't be mistaken for new requests. No transparent retry within a request.
- `verify_stripe_checksums` can be enabled server-side to enforce per-stripe checksum validation (requires rewriting tested objects).
- Hard limit of **32 configured routes** caps per-request QP/worker creation.

### Measured Performance
| Result | Value | Context |
|---|---|---|
| Same-plan direct vs packed-contiguous RXE throughput | **1.100×** (64 MiB), **1.161×** (256 MiB) | Software RXE, ten process blocks per size |
| Generation-transition witness (Oct 12) | 8 rejected direct reads with strictly increasing Generations | Single-writer setup |
| Oct 16 live capture | 64 MiB write/read, matching single/dual-rail hashes, genuine baseline late-WRITE corruption, fixed-buffer recovery, 3 PUT/GET recovery rounds | Demo |
| KVService cold reads (not RailFuse-specific) | 6.4–8.8 GB/s per stream, 23 GB/s aggregate at 8 streams | 2 nodes × 2 NVMe |

### Explicit Evidence Boundaries (important)
The README is unusually careful about what RailFuse **does not** prove:
- Software-RoCE (RXE) results do **not** establish **physical dual-HCA aggregation** or end-to-end inference speedup.
- Physical two-HCA rail runs were **not run** (only one HCA port online on available nodes).
- The mock benchmark numbers are **host-specific software measurements**, not RDMA hardware results.
- The state explorer and Verbs fail-stop shim are **test-only**, not provider/implementation proofs.
- Server commit timing and in-flight RDMA WRITE state during rewrite races remain **unmeasured**.
- Prior art acknowledged: **Mooncake (FAST '25)** multi-NIC transfer; RailFuse's narrow contribution is the versioned object/failure contract + controlled reduction in software staging cost.

### How to Try It
- Benchmark CLI: `cs-rail-read-bench` (with `--rail` manual mapping or `--local-rail` discovery mode)
- Reproducible Soft-RoCE setup: `kv-service/deploy/softroce-vm/` builds two Ubuntu 22.04 KVM guests with 4 RXE devices (two rails each), no production NIC attached
- Collectors: `collect_rail_verbs.py`, `collect_rail_concurrent.py`, `collect_rail_modes.py`; auditor: `audit_rail_modes.py`
- Tests: `cargo test --features rdma rail_read::tests` (plus ignored real-hardware `rail_read_e2e` suite with fault-injection env vars)

---

**Bottom line:** RailFuse is a bandwidth-multiplying RDMA read path for striped KV-cache objects, using multiple local NICs to read one object from one storage node — with a rigorously documented safety contract and honestly-scoped performance evidence (software RoCE only, no physical multi-HCA claim).

看完 10 个项目，我的第一判断是：**这份名单实质上是一张 Agent 基础设施的分层地图，并非 10 个“AI 应用”的集合**。除了 NuwaX 稍微偏向平台产品，其余项目都在补齐模型以下的那一层。

| 项目 | 所处层次 | 一句话 | 我判断的护城河、软肋 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ShannonBase | 数据底座 | 把向量、ML、LLM、Agent 塞进 MySQL 内核 | 真 fork 内核 + Rapid 列存；但上游合并负担重、GPL、缺公开硬 benchmark |
| 女娲 NuwaX | Agent 平台 | 可自托管的 Agent OS：创建、发布、运营，以及沙箱、IM 渠道 | 交付完整度、信创适配；但和 Dify、Coze 正面竞争，差异没讲清 |
| Kestrel-LLM | 端侧推理 | 纯 C11、1.4MB、ARM 上跑 Qwen3-VL 与 30B-A3B | 手写 NEON、VQF、分层流式；但单平台、单模型族、单人维护 |
| fde mcp blade | 工具接入治理 | 机房里的 MCP 网关：五重安全、全链路审计、插件 | 场景切口极准；技术不深，容易被平台厂商内置 |
| Mega2 | 代码/制品底座 | Rust 的 trunk-based monorepo + Git/LFS/OCI + Agent Session Capture | 存储引擎 + 前作积累；开源版砍掉 UI、CL，更像引流版 |
| SME | 记忆算法 | 带遗忘、强化、区域的空间记忆引擎 | 记忆动力学 + 可解释 + 中文离线；赛道极挤、自建评测 |
| Morphz | Agent 运行时 | 把 context 变成版本化事务对象，模型只负责语义 | 全场最原创的抽象；0.1 预览、Yao 语言、生态为零 |
| 层迹 LayerTrace | AI 可观测 | 以 VM 为边界的跨层故障诊断 + 证据链 | 证据链与恢复验证扎实；绑定 ZSvirt、规则式诊断 |
| MatrixHub 安全 | 模型供应链 | 模型制品隔离扫描 + 版本绑定准入 | 证据可复现、准入闭环完整；引擎靠第三方、扫描性能一般 |
| RailFuse | KV 存储数据面 | ContextStore 上多网卡 RDMA 并行读 | 安全契约与 fail-stop 设计；增益仅 10–16%、依赖上游 |

## 四个我认为值得讨论的观察

**1. 六个项目其实在解决同一个问题：状态。**
ShannonBase 管 DB 状态，ContextStore/RailFuse 管 KV 状态，SME 管记忆状态，Morphz 管 context 状态，Mega2 管代码与 session 状态，NuwaX 管会话与知识状态。LLM 本身无状态、应用必须有状态，这是这一届的主旋律。但六家切在完全不同的层：物理层（KV 块）、算法层（记忆）、语义层（context 对象）、平台层（会话）。**我的判断是这一层最终只会留下 2–3 个标准**，KV 物理层大概率被 vLLM/LMCache 吸收，记忆算法会被平台内置，只有“结构化 context 运行时”有可能长成新抽象，但 Morphz 太早了。

**2. 三种团队气质，不能用同一把尺评。**
- 产品型：NuwaX、fde-blade，README 就是卖点，完成度高；
- 系统型：ShannonBase、Kestrel、Mega2、ContextStore/RailFuse，拼内核、协议、性能；
- 研究型：Morphz、SME、LayerTrace、MatrixHub，拼抽象、证据、边界。

用“star 数”评系统型会低估，用“能不能装起来”评研究型会误伤。

**3. 证据质量是最被低估的维度，这四家应该加分。**
Kestrel 主动撤回不可复现的历史数据集；SME 在 README 里自我证伪了 region 的归因（0–1pp，落在噪声内）；RailFuse 明确写“物理双 HCA 未测、端到端推理增益未测”；MatrixHub 自己说 794 条断言不等于 794 个攻击样本。这种“自曝边界”在比赛材料里非常罕见。反过来，有些项目给的是能力清单，不是可复现结果——建议追问一句：**能否一条命令复现，且基线与你们同配置？**

**4. “参赛作品”和“开源项目”要分开看。**
MatrixHub、LayerTrace、RailFuse 的交付物极重（29 页报告、224 秒视频、断言计数、复现脚本），这是赛题要求，不等于社区可维护性。RailFuse 本质是 ContextStore 的一个 research 分支，没合回上游；MatrixHub 是贡献快照，不是官方发行版；Mega2 开源版是 storage-only。三个都有“材料完成度 > 开源完成度”的特征。顺便说一句：名单里 RailFuse 的链接少了一个 `f`，真实 commit 是 `3fe4b26d72fff...`，现在点开是 404。

## 如果按维度投票，我会这么分

- **技术密度**：Kestrel ≈ ShannonBase > RailFuse > Mega2
- **开源影响力潜力**：SME > Kestrel > fde-blade
- **企业落地速度**：fde-blade > NuwaX > MatrixHub
- **抽象创新**：Morphz，遥遥领先，但也最可能变成一篇好论文
- **最被低估**：LayerTrace——AI workload 的跨层诊断是真需求，只是被“绑定 ZSvirt”掩盖了通用价值
- **最被高估**：NuwaX——功能面太宽，微前端、沙箱、IM、ACP 每一项都有更强对手，建议收缩到“信创私有化 Agent 交付”一个点

## 想听你的判断

1. 这次评的是**开源项目**还是**参赛作品**？这直接决定 MatrixHub/RailFuse/LayerTrace 该不该压过 SME/Kestrel。
2. 记忆/上下文这五家（SME、Morphz、ContextStore、NuwaX、ShannonBase），你觉得会收敛到哪一层？我倾向上面的“三层分化”判断。
3. 你更想看哪个方向的深挖：**技术尽调**（读代码、验 benchmark）、**赛道卡位**（和 Mem0/Dify/LMCache 对比）、还是**评分框架**（给评委用的维度与权重）？

告诉我你的身份（评委/组织方/参赛者/投资），我可以把分析换成对应的视角。

**1. 这批项目整体还没有“破圈”。** 10 个项目里没有一个达到 1k 星，一半不到 30 星。这是一个“早期项目池”，并非“明星项目池”——不能拿它跟 Mem0（上万星）或 Dify（数万星）放在同一坐标系里。

**2. 星数与技术密度几乎无关。** Kestrel 只有 29 星，却是全场工程密度最高的项目之一；NuwaX 有 895 星，但它的功能面最宽、护城河最浅。星数更多反映“曝光 + 产品可试用性”，技术深度更像“评委该看的东西”。这也是我上一轮说“不能用一把尺”的原因。

**3. 三个企业赛题几乎零独立星数。** MatrixHub 1★、LayerTrace 0★、RailFuse 0★，它们真正继承的是上游的热度：MatrixHub 上游 356★、ContextStore 上游 11★、Mega 前作 539★（已归档，Mega2 只剩 32★）。这印证了“参赛作品 ≠ 开源项目”——它们的社区是借来的，不是自己长出来的。

**4. 比 star 更诚实的指标是 issue 数和 fork 深度。** SME、Kestrel、LayerTrace、MatrixHub 的 open issue 全是 0，说明还没有真实外部用户在使用；而 MatrixHub 上游有 244 个 open issue，那才是“有人在用”的信号。NuwaX 180 个 fork、ShannonBase 25 个 fork 属于正常比例；Mega2 只有 3 个 fork，说明“看的人多、跑的人少”。

**5. Gitee 的 29 星不等于 GitHub 的 29 星。** Gitee 星数的池子和曝光机制小得多，Kestrel 若同步到 GitHub，数字大概率会变；反过来，Gitee 上也更容易出现“互星”。跨平台排名要谨慎。

要不要我拉一下 star 曲线（star-history）？**一条平滑上升线是自然增长，一个台阶是一次曝光/推文，一条平线就是“发完没人看”**——这比总数更能判断这几个项目的真实热度。

中国研究生操作系统开源创新大赛(简称“大赛”)是中国研究生创新实践系列大赛主题赛事之一,是面向研究生和本科生的全国性、公益性开源创新赛。大赛坚持以国家战略需求为导向,以夯实基础软件生态、强化人才培养为目标,围绕操作系统关键技术和生态建设,激发研究生创新意识,提升研究生创新与实践能力,着力培养创新型、复合型、应用型高端人才,为操作系统生态健康发展提供人才支撑。大赛由教育部学位管理与研究生教育司指导、中国学位与研究生教育学会主办,大赛组委会秘书处单位设在国防科技大学。2026年第三届中国研究生操作系统开源创新大赛暨开放原子大赛操作系统专项赛由清华大学承办,开放原子开源基金会作为战略合作单位,OpenAtom openKylin(以下简称“openKylin”)社区等作为赞助单位。10月15日至17日,第三届中国研究生操作系统开源创新大赛暨开放原子大赛操作系统专项赛决赛在北京格兰云天国际酒店与清华大学隆重举行,中国工程院院士孙家广、中国科学院院士王怀民,以及清华大学党委副书记、副校长白本锋,国防科技大学副校长吴建军,中国学位与研究生教育学会副会长郭新立等领导嘉宾出席并致辞。在同期举行的「开源筑基·智启未来——2026开源人才发展大会」上,openKylin社区资深专家、麒麟软件有限公司总经理孔金珠作《智能操作系统的发展与思考》特邀报告,回顾了操作系统从大型机时代到智能体时代的演进历程,指出智能原生操作系统将成为下一代基础软件底座,并分享了openKylin在智能操作系统研究与探索方面的实践与思考。本届大赛分为系统创新、应用创新、研究创新三大赛道,共有来自112所研究生培养单位的483支队伍报名,大赛专家评审组秉承公平公正的原则进行了严格评审,共有108支队伍晋级决赛。决赛期间,参赛队伍先后完成现场报到、分组答辩与公开路演。经过为期三天的激烈角逐,大赛结果正式揭晓:共产生12支一等奖队伍(含冠、亚、季军各1支),21支二等奖队伍,72支三等奖队伍。10月17日上午,晋级一等奖的队伍进行公开路演,由现场专家评审公开打分与投票,产生冠、亚、季军各一名。openKylin赛题队伍再创佳绩——来自国防科技大学、赛题为“面向openKylin的智能体记忆提取与精准遗忘机制”的“Memoryd”队伍勇夺亚军,续写openKylin社区在赛事中的优异表现!同样来自国防科技大学、赛题为“面向多智能体的操作系统级执行时(Agent Runtime)”的“想露一手”队伍,基于openKylin系统完成项目研发,斩获季军!再次恭喜以上获奖队伍!感谢各位参赛同学与指导老师们的全力以赴与坚守付出,愿大家在开源创新的道路上不断探索,保持热爱,勇攀高峰!中国研究生操作系统开源创新大赛已成为我国操作系统领域人才培养的重要平台。通过「以赛促研、以赛育人」的模式,大赛为操作系统生态健康发展提供了人才支撑。openKylin社区作为中国开源操作系统的重要力量,将持续支持中国研究生操作系统开源创新大赛,并不断推出更多开源赛事,进一步搭建「产学研用」协同育人平台,推动高校与开源社区、企业的深度合作,为我国操作系统领域持续输送高素质人才,助力基础软件产业高质量发展。往期推荐:内核跃迁,智能原生 | openKylin 3.0 正式发布祝贺!openKylin技术委员会主任吴庆波荣获2026年"CCF王选奖"外交部公布: openKylin入选上合成果清单,重塑全球基础软件合作新范式UKUI 4.24:“看得见”的新变化OpenAtom openKylin是由开放原子开源基金会孵化及运营的开源项目,由基础软硬件企业、非营利性组织、社团组织、高等院校、科研机构和个人开发者共同创立。社区以“为世界提供与人工智能技术深度融合的开源操作系统”为愿景,旨在于开源、自愿、平等、协作的基础上,共同打造全球领先的智能操作系统开源根社区,推动Linux开源技术及其软硬件生态繁荣发展。

顺带提醒：早期通稿里写的是“10 月 24 日总决赛”，官网已改成 **10 月 29 日**，以官网为准。

## 现在能确定的信息

- **奖项盘子**：三赛道独立评奖。基础奖每赛道 10 个（一等 1 / 二等 2 / 三等 3 / 优秀 4），共 30 个；特设奖 27 个（最佳探索 12、潜力新锐 10、遗珠 5）；合计 57 个名额，100 万奖池，现金与 Token 各半。
- **不重复获奖**，同一项目取最高等级。
- 评审权重：技术创新 30%、场景落地 30%、开源治理 20%、长期发展 20%。

## 一个推断

你截图那 10 个项目，大概率是**智算云赛道**的入围名单——因为三个企业赛题（ZSvirt 的层迹、DaoCloud 的 MatrixHub 与 RailFuse）全在智算云赛道，其余 7 个也都是基础设施类项目。另外两个赛道（AI+工业软件、开源 AI 工具）应该各有约 10 个项目，合计 30 个左右。

如果这个推断成立，意味着**这 10 个项目已经人手一个奖**（10 个入围对 10 个基础奖），29 号只是决定谁拿一等、谁拿优秀，以及能不能再叠加特设奖。这对上一轮的判断有影响：在这条赛道里，真正的悬念不是“能不能获奖”，而是“一等奖 10 万归谁”。

29 号之后要我再去官网和 OSC 新闻里捞一遍获奖名单吗？也可以现在先把三个赛道的完整入围名单找齐，做个交叉对比。
